system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranty cap: 20% of price (A$4.8m). | Higher general cap, ideally 30–50%, with separate uncapped/price-cap categories. | **Reject as sole regime; seek ≥30% general cap.** Known operational, customer and compliance risks could exceed A$4.8m. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | A$25k de minimis; A$250k deductible basket; only excess recoverable. | Lower de minimis and tipping basket, or no basket for identified/indemnified matters. | **Seek A$10k de minimis and A$100k tipping basket; exclude indemnities/fundamental/tax claims.** The proposed thresholds can suppress multiple related losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | Notify within 18 months; limitations purportedly apply to all claims. | At least 24 months for business warranties; longer survival for tax, IP, privacy/data and fundamental claims. | **Reject universal 18-month period.** Several risks may crystallise after 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to ordinary cap and time limit. | Title, capacity, authority and share ownership warranties uncapped or capped at 100% of price, with long survival. | **Reject.** Buyer must retain meaningful recourse if it does not receive the shares free of competing interests. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all claims; no express fraud carve-out identified. | Express carve-out for fraud, fraudulent concealment and wilful misconduct, including preservation of statutory rights to the extent permitted. | **Add express carve-out.** The current “all Claims” drafting could improperly constrain remedies for dishonest conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Fair, specific disclosure only: identify the warranty, material/facts, consequences and supporting documents; no broad data-room/public-record deeming provision. | **Delete or materially narrow general disclosure.** A document dump shifts disclosure risk to Buyer and obscures whether a warranty is actually qualified. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer/advisers or discoverable from data room/public records. | Limit to Buyer’s actual knowledge of specified senior deal personnel, acquired before signing, and only where expressly and fairly disclosed. | **Delete “discoverable” and adviser-wide knowledge language.** Constructive knowledge undermines negotiated warranties and rewards inadequate disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; treats condition satisfied on written consent; no final consent or proof conditions met. Bluefen is ~A$3.6m / 30% FY26 revenue. | Consent as a Completion condition, in form satisfactory to Buyer, with all conditions satisfied or accepted by Buyer; termination/right to defer and specific indemnity or holdback. | **Make Bluefen a Buyer-controlled CP and obtain protection if unresolved.** Loss or conditional impairment of a 30% revenue customer is material. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | ~A$3.2m facility not repaid; release/security discharge only following Completion. | Repayment and irrevocable release/discharge at or before Completion through funds flow; no Buyer/company liability or residual security. | **Require simultaneous Completion payoff and releases.** A post-Completion release leaves Buyer owning a leveraged company and exposed to enforcement risk. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | A$420k conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller-funded payment or price reduction/escrow covering bonuses plus super, payroll tax and all employment on-costs; clear treatment in Completion accounts. | **Treat as seller leakage/debt-like item unless expressly priced.** The undisclosed total liability exceeds the stated A$420k. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; A$180k remains open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Specific indemnity for ownership, use and infringement exposure, plus pre-Completion payment and written assignment/waiver confirmation; escrow/retention pending evidence. | **Expand indemnity and require evidence before Completion.** Non-payment may prevent transfer of project materials/IP essential to the business. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary matter; no confirmed access, scope, notification requirement or loss; Seller says not expected material. | Full investigation, containment and remediation before Completion; disclosure of results; regulatory/third-party notification compliance; specific uncapped or separately capped indemnity and holdback. | **Do not accept “preliminary” as resolution.** The incident may create privacy, contractual, regulatory and reputational liabilities after Completion. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling A$330k characterised as ordinary-course costs; terms/avoidability/accrual not stated. | Copies and confirmation of term, termination rights, commencement, accrual and approval; treat non-ordinary/prepaid or post-Completion committed costs as leakage/price adjustment where appropriate. | **Keep open pending document review.** “Ordinary course” does not establish that the commitments are necessary, terminable or properly reflected in price. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Seller seeks one general limitations/non-reliance regime for all claims. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, restrictive covenants and fraud. | **Insist on category-specific caps, baskets and survival periods.** A universal regime strips protection from risks inherently different from ordinary warranty claims. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller owns 100%; states Buyer must conduct its own verification. | Completion deliverables confirming clean title: original/valid share certificates if applicable, executed transfers, board approvals, updated register, ASIC searches and releases of all security/interests. | **Require affirmative title warranty and closing evidence.** A register alone does not establish absence of encumbrances, competing claims or transfer defects. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP are settled under the general regime. | Standalone tax covenant/indemnity with tax-specific survival (typically through statutory limitation period plus buffer), and enhanced IP warranties/indemnity with longer survival and separate cap. | **Reject treatment under the general regime.** Tax and IP liabilities are potentially material, latent and not suitable for an 18-month/20% general-warranty package. |
=== END ADVICE ===
